recorded: 2026-09-27, gfx1151 Strix Halo (zbook), Q4_K grouped-prefill fetch strategy
candidate: the Q4_K grouped expert prefill stages the expert's activation rows in shared memory (read from L2 once per eight output columns instead of once per column) and hoists each output column's d*scale and dmin*min pairs into shared memory per 32-element sub-block (one byte load and two flops in the inner loop instead of re-extracting the metadata per weight element)
reason: fresh attribution on the post-weight-reuse tree showed the grouped kernels were still 68% of prefill kernel time while moving only ~4 GB/s of weight bytes, so the cost was fetch, not bandwidth: at the artifact's geometry 30 ms of the 49 ms went to the Q4_K dequant and 21 ms to the activation-side FMA. Both are exact rewrites of the same expressions - (d*scale)*q - (dmin*min) with the same two products, and the same per-thread k-partition - so the fix costs no numerical budget and needed no gate exemption.

attribution.method: rocprofv3 --kernel-trace over one 512-token prefill on the post-weight-reuse tree (scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py --prompt 512 --output 1 --samples 1 --warmup 0), kernel time summed by kernel name
attribution.reading: the two expert projections are still 68% of prefill kernel time after the weight reuse, which is what falsified the assumption that removing the weight re-read was the whole story

isolation.method: scratch probes at the artifact geometry (in 2816, out 1408, 128 experts, 4096 compact rows, 272 MiB of Q4_K weights), each dropping one component so the remainder could be timed; not committed
isolation.reading: ~30 ms dequant, ~21 ms activation-side, ~4 ms staging: two fetch problems, neither of them the weight read

mechanism.rewrite: activation rows staged in shared memory per (row batch, k-chunk), so the block's activation bytes are read from L2 once per OUT_TILE output columns; per-sub-block d*scale and dmin*min precomputed into shared by the first 64 threads; activations held in registers across the output tile; reduction untouched
mechanism.bit_exactness: the per-thread k-partition (k = threadIdx.x, threadIdx.x + 128, ... in ascending order), the 32-lane shfl tree and thread 0's wave-total sum are the shipped kernel's, and the metadata hoist is the same two products in the same order, so outputs are bit-identical rather than within tolerance

correctness.gate: scripts/gemma4_teacher_forced_gate.py gate --baseline /tmp/gemma4-gate-strict-gfx1151.npz --prompt 2048 --prefill 1024, 1023 teacher-forced rows at keys 1025-2047 with the decode split engaged (30690 split launches), chain_sha256 matching the baseline: kl_mean 0.0, kl_p95 0.0, kl_p99 0.0, kl_max 0.0, top-1 rate 1.0 with zero flips, passed true, failed []
correctness.bit_exactness_test: tests/test_unit_gemma4_expert_route.py asserts bit-identical bf16 outputs against the selected GEMV for every grouped variant a quant registers - the staged one and the plain one for Q4_K, the plain one for Q5_1 - across 10 quant/geometry cases including the artifact's own (1408, 2816) gate/up
correctness.kernel_level: the scratch micro-harness compared the staged kernel against the shipped grouped kernel on 5,767,168 bf16 outputs at the artifact geometry: 0 differ
correctness.preference_order: two tests cover the route's new ordered variant list: the preferred variant is taken when both are registered, and a quant that registers only the later one still runs it
correctness.generation_parity: both arms emit identical greedy ids at 512/128 and report public_path_parity true
